nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The developer/orchestrator who runs the recovery CLIs (es-merge, es-generate, demo) and launches es-view. Here they invoke the merge to fold a directory of per-flow trace JSONs into the one canonical, validated model.

nodes.label: Per-flow trace JSON
nodes.description: A single per-flow trace document authored by a deep-trace agent: { nodes, flows, hotspots, terms } for one flow. Every such file in the traces directory is the raw material the merge consumes; a parse failure is collected and the file skipped rather than aborting the run.

tactical.explanation: readTraceDocs (the fs adapter, src/adapters/fs/model-repository.ts) reads every *.json in the directory (sorted) and JSON.parses each into a { doc, name } source; an unparseable file becomes a parseError and is skipped, not fatal. mergeTraceDocs (the pure domain merge, src/domain/model/merge.ts) then iterates each source's doc.nodes / doc.flows / doc.hotspots / doc.terms. This read model is what the command projects from the trace files on disk; the fs read and the pure merge are now separate modules (ports-and-adapters split).

anchors.note: readdirSync + filter *.json, sorted
JSON.parse each file into a source doc; parse errors collected, file skipped
iterate each source doc's nodes/flows/hotspots/terms

nodes.label: MergeTraces
nodes.description: Fold every per-flow trace document into one canonical, validated model: union shared nodes by global id, accumulate flows/hotspots/terms, compute derived meta, and check every invariant before the model is returned to the caller.

tactical.explanation: A deterministic ETL transform kept in a single plane per the two-plane rule (parse/seed/union/validate stages are NOT promoted to aggregates/policies/events). The refactor made the command boundary explicit: mergeTraces (src/application/commands/merge-traces.ts) is now the application-layer command handler — it reads the trace dir through the ModelRepository port (readTraceDocs), delegates to the pure domain mergeTraceDocs (src/domain/model/merge.ts) for the seed/union/validate/build pipeline, and returns { model, errors, warnings, files }. mergeTraceDocs itself: (1) SEEDS/UNIONS nodes into a Map keyed by global id: first-seen type/label wins; longest description wins; ownedBy / synchronous / inferred-false / physical attrs (parent, storeKind, fieldKind, dataType, host, engine, nullable) fill forward; fields[] union by name (a later data-pass trace is authoritative on a field); provenance set-unioned; each source's tactical block appended as a per-flow `usages` entry. (2) flows deduped by id, hotspots/terms deduped keeping first. (3) VALIDATE against every invariant (crossValidate, src/domain/model/invariants.ts), accumulating errors[] and warnings[]. (4) Build the model with derived meta. The CLI (src/adapters/cli/es-merge.ts, runMerge) owns IO: writes flows.json via writeModelFile and maps errors to exit 1; resolveModel (src/application/commands/resolve-model.ts) throws on errors so the server never serves an invalid model.

anchors.note: application command: read trace dir via the ModelRepository port, delegate to mergeTraceDocs
pure domain: seed/union nodes, accumulate flows, validate, build model
CLI front end: argv, writeModelFile, exit codes
in-memory --traces path; throws on any validation error

nodes.label: The Model
nodes.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): the deduped node set plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta (counts, shared-concept glossary, dead-flow index). Built by the merge, then read by the es-view server and the DOT/explorer generator. Its invariants ARE the merge-time validation rules.

tactical.explanation: Assembled in mergeTraceDocs (src/domain/model/merge.ts) as { version:1, meta:{ generatedFrom, counts, deadFlows, sharedGlossary }, nodes, flows, hotspots, terms }. Internal transient keys (_src on nodes, _sourceFile on flows) are stripped on output. Its state lives in a file on the CLI path (writeModelFile) or purely in memory on the server --traces path. The refactor extracted an explicit Model aggregate class (src/domain/model/model.ts) wrapping the same nodes/flows/hotspots/terms/meta shape with a validate() method that re-runs crossValidate — the identical invariant checks — for callers that already hold a resolved model rather than raw traces. The whole validation block is this aggregate's invariant enforcement; the derived-meta block computes the shared glossary and dead-flow index it exposes.

anchors.note: the assembled model object
strip transient _src/_sourceFile keys on output
explicit Model aggregate class wrapping the same data + validate()

fields.name: meta.sharedGlossary
fields.derivation: Every node id that appears in more than one flow (across steps and edge from/to), projected to { id, type, label, description, flowCount, flows } and sorted by flowCount desc. This is how independent flows are shown to join into one map.

fields.name: meta.deadFlows
fields.derivation: The dead-flow index: every flow whose status is not 'live', projected to { id, status, supersededBy, name }. Regenerable, not hand-authored.

fields.name: meta.counts.byType
fields.derivation: Node count grouped by node type, plus totals for flows/nodes/hotspots/terms and a count of unresolved terms.

evidence.note: typeCounts accumulated over nodes; counts assembled into meta

nodes.label: Every id reference resolves and ids are unique
nodes.description: The model must be a closed graph: nodes are well-formed with a known type and a unique id, and every reference (flow steps, edge from/to, flow hotspots, term relatedNodes) points at a defined node. Dangling references or id collisions are ERRORS that fail the merge. (Orphan nodes and nonstandard edge verbs are only warnings.)

tactical.explanation: ERROR-level checks: a node needs id+type+label and a type in NODE_TYPES (merge.ts 33-34); re-seeing an id with a different type is a type conflict (merge.ts 45); a duplicate flow id is rejected keeping the first (merge.ts 72); each flow step must resolve (invariants.ts crossValidate 87); each edge.from/edge.to must resolve (invariants.ts 88-89); each flow hotspot must be defined (invariants.ts 93). WARNING-level companions in the same blocks: a duplicate hotspot/term id keeps the first (merge.ts 77, 83), a nonstandard edge verb (invariants.ts 90), a missing flow kind/status (invariants.ts 85-86), an unknown supersededBy flow (invariants.ts 94), and orphan nodes referenced by no flow (invariants.ts 128). The node-shape checks stayed in the merge pipeline (merge.ts); the cross-reference checks moved into the dedicated invariants module (invariants.ts) shared by the Model aggregate's validate().

anchors.note: cross-reference block: steps/edges/hotspots resolve (83-94)
node needs id+type+label; type must be in NODE_TYPES
type conflict on re-seen node id
duplicate flow id rejected

nodes.label: Aggregates never issue commands
nodes.description: The one hard Event Storming grammar rule enforced at merge time: an aggregate may only receive commands and emit events, never issue one. An edge whose from-node is an aggregate with verb 'issues' is an ERROR. Policies-issue-commands and command-lookup shapes are left to author discipline.

tactical.explanation: After cross-reference validation, every flow edge is scanned: if the from-node resolves to type 'aggregate' and the verb is exactly 'issues', it is pushed as an error. This is the only ES-grammar constraint the merge actively enforces; the schema's other grammar rules (policies are strictly reactive, invariants attach to aggregates, UI-vs-service split) are documented but NOT validated here. Now lives in crossValidate (src/domain/model/invariants.ts), shared by both the merge pipeline and the Model aggregate's validate().

anchors.note: scan edges; aggregate + verb 'issues' => forbidden (98-103)

nodes.label: Terms are resolved-with-definition or flagged-with-a-question
nodes.description: Every ubiquitous-language term must be well-formed and honor the flag-or-resolve contract: a resolved term carries a definition; a partial/unresolved term carries the specific openQuestion a human should answer; and any relatedNodes must resolve to known nodes. Violations are ERRORS. A nonstandard category is only a warning.

tactical.explanation: ERROR-level: a term needs id+term (merge.ts 82); status must be in {resolved, partial, unresolved} (invariants.ts 109); a resolved term needs a non-empty definition (invariants.ts 111); a non-resolved status requires a non-empty openQuestion (invariants.ts 112); every relatedNodes id must resolve (invariants.ts 113). WARNING-level: a nonstandard category (invariants.ts 110) and a duplicate term id keeping the first (merge.ts 83). No terms flow through this particular merge trace, but the contract still guards any term-bearing source doc.

anchors.note: status/definition/openQuestion contract + relatedNodes resolve (107-113)
term needs id+term; duplicate id keeps first (82-83)

nodes.label: Physical containment and field lineage are well-formed
nodes.description: The data-model layer must be internally consistent: a physical node's parent must resolve and form an acyclic containment chain, and each field must carry a non-empty name and derivation with any local-looking source ref resolving to a known node. Violations are ERRORS; a parent at the wrong containment level is only a warning (it is silently dropped from the tree).

tactical.explanation: ERROR-level: a node's parent must be a known node (invariants.ts 66-68) and the parent chain must be acyclic, caught by a walk-up with a seen-set (invariants.ts 74-76); each field needs a non-empty name and derivation (invariants.ts 34-37, validateFields); a field source ref matching /^(ds|fld)-/ must resolve to a known node (invariants.ts 43). WARNING-level: a parent at the wrong containment level per PARENT_LEVEL (datastore parents a datastore; a field parents a datastore or field) is dropped from the tree, not rejected (invariants.ts 71); nonstandard field confidence/role/transform and non-boolean conceptual are warnings (invariants.ts 38-42). validateFields is now its own exported function, called once per node from crossValidate.

anchors.note: parent resolves + acyclic chain + wrong-level warning (64-80)
field name+derivation required; local source ref /^(ds|fld)-/ must resolve (31-46)
allowed parent types per node type

nodes.label: Behavioral nodes carry source anchors
nodes.description: A soft (WARNING-only) invariant: nodes of an anchor-required type (command, aggregate, event, policy, readModel, invariant) should carry at least one tactical.anchor, so the recovered concept always deep-links back to code. Unlike the referential and grammar rules this does NOT fail the merge; it only surfaces a warning.

tactical.explanation: During the node loop in mergeTraceDocs, if a node's type is in ANCHOR_REQUIRED and it lacks a non-empty tactical.anchors array, a warning is pushed. Modeled as a distinct invariant to make the error-vs-warning boundary explicit: this is the clearest example of a validation the merge performs but does not enforce as a gate. The ANCHOR_REQUIRED set itself now lives beside the other validation enums in invariants.ts.

anchors.note: ANCHOR_REQUIRED type with no tactical.anchors => warning (35-36)
the set of node types expected to carry anchors

nodes.label: ModelMerged
nodes.description: The per-flow traces have been folded into one deduped model: shared nodes unioned by global id, flows/hotspots/terms accumulated, and derived meta (counts, shared-concept glossary, dead-flow index) computed. This fact holds even when the model is later found invalid.

tactical.explanation: Realized by the node-union loop (seed new id / merge re-seen id) plus the derived-meta block that builds sharedGlossary (ids appearing in >1 flow), deadFlows (status != live), and typeCounts. This is the domain-significant fact promoted out of the seed/union pipeline stages, which stay inside cmd-merge-traces tactical. mergeTraceDocs ALWAYS returns a model object here, independently of whether validation later finds errors.

anchors.note: node union: seed new / merge re-seen
derived meta: sharedGlossary + deadFlows + counts

nodes.label: ModelValidated
nodes.description: The merged model has been checked against every invariant and passed with zero errors, so it is safe to serve or persist. When errors exist this fact does NOT hold: the CLI reports them and exits nonzero, and the server throws and refuses to serve. It is a separately-observable outcome from ModelMerged (a model can be merged-but-invalid).

tactical.explanation: The validation loops (crossValidate, src/domain/model/invariants.ts) accumulate an errors[] array; an empty array is the validated fact. runMerge (es-merge.ts) prints 'validation: OK' only when errors.length === 0 (otherwise it has already written the file, then exits 1); resolveModel (resolve-model.ts) throws when merged.errors.length so the in-memory server path never exposes an unvalidated model. Because 'merged' always happens but 'validated' only when clean, the two are modeled as distinct events with separate outcome windows.

anchors.note: crossValidate call: start of the validation blocks that populate errors[]
'validation: OK' only when no errors
throw on any validation error so the server serves nothing (37-40)

nodes.label: Local filesystem
nodes.description: The local filesystem outside the process, reached through node:fs. Holds the per-flow trace JSONs read as input and receives the merged flows.json written as output. The in-memory --traces server path reads but never writes it.

tactical.explanation: Accessed via node:fs in the fs adapter (src/adapters/fs/model-repository.ts): readTraceDocs does readdirSync + readFileSync of *.json inputs, and writeModelFile does fs.writeFileSync(outFile, ...) to persist the result. runMerge (es-merge.ts) is the CLI front end that calls writeModelFile.

anchors.note: node:fs is the filesystem boundary

nodes.label: traces/ directory
nodes.description: The input directory of per-flow trace JSONs (the tracesDir argument to es-merge, or the --traces dir for es-view). Every *.json in it is read, sorted, and merged.

tactical.explanation: readTraceDocs enumerates it with fs.readdirSync and keeps files ending in .json, sorted for deterministic order.

anchors.note: readdirSync(dir).filter(.json).sort()

nodes.label: <flow-id>.json (per-flow trace)
nodes.description: One per-flow trace file on disk: { nodes, flows, hotspots, terms } authored by a deep-trace agent. Source material the merge parses; rm-trace is the in-memory projection of it.

tactical.explanation: Each file is read with fs.readFileSync and JSON.parsed into a { doc, name } source; an unparseable file is collected as a parseError and skipped.

anchors.note: JSON.parse(readFileSync(file)) per trace file

nodes.label: flows.json (canonical model)
nodes.description: The output canonical model written by the es-merge CLI. Consumed downstream by the es-view server and the DOT/explorer generator. On the in-memory --traces server path this file is never written; the model is held in memory only.

tactical.explanation: runMerge (src/adapters/cli/es-merge.ts) calls writeModelFile(outFile, model), which serializes the merged model with JSON.stringify(model, null, 2) and fs.writeFileSync (src/adapters/fs/model-repository.ts). Note it is written BEFORE the error check, so a failed validation still leaves a file on disk.

anchors.note: writeFileSync(outFile, JSON.stringify(model))

flows.name: Operator merges per-flow traces into the validated model
flows.summary: The operator runs es-merge (or es-view --traces) over a directory of per-flow trace JSONs. The tool reads every trace file, unions the shared nodes by global id and accumulates the flows, hotspots, and terms into one canonical model, computes derived meta (shared glossary, dead-flow index, counts), then validates the whole graph against its invariants. On success it writes (CLI) or holds in memory (server) the validated flows.json the server and generator consume; on any error the CLI writes-then-flags-and-exits-1 while the server throws and serves nothing. The point is to let independent trace agents converge on one consistent, referentially closed model.
flows.trigger: Operator runs `node dist/node/adapters/cli/cli.js merge <tracesDir> <outFile>` (the unified CLI's `merge` subcommand — cli.ts, backed by es-merge.ts's runMerge), or es-view resolves a model from `--traces <dir>`.
